_about: Golden cases for how a sender resolves mentions into a frame's `m` (people) and `ma` (everyone).
Normative: docs/sealed-messages.md §Keys of a frame (keys `m` and `ma`).

The spec requires only that `m` be resolved by the sender against the roster. This table pins how the official clients do it, and a sender SHOULD match it so that every client highlights the same names.

A handle is `[a-z0-9_]{3,30}` after `@`, matched case-insensitively, not preceded by `[a-z0-9_@/]` and not followed by `[a-z0-9_]`. Handles are lowercased, deduplicated, kept in body order and capped at 10 people. Only members of the conversation resolve.
`@all` sets `everyone` in a group and is plain text in a two-person conversation. It never appears in `mentions`.
`roster` is the conversation's members as {id, handle}. Each `resolve` case gives a `body` and `isGroup`, and `expect` gives `mentions` as [{userId, handle}] (the frame's `u` and `h`) and `everyone`.
To replay: run each case through your own implementation of the format and compare the result with the case's expectation, field by field.

resolve.name: case-insensitive, lowercased, deduplicated, in body order
@all in a group is everyone and names nobody
@all in a DM is just text
a handle that is not in the chat is text
a longer word starting with a handle is not that handle
a DM still resolves the other person's handle
